Marks: **(M1)** method, **(A1)** accuracy, **(B1)** independent. Total **36**.

Two habits to check: with a modulus, did they **split by sign** (never $\int|g|=|\int g|$)? With a definite
integral inside a definition, did they name it $k$ and **use symmetry** ($\int_{-a}^{a}\text{odd}=0$) to finish?

# Section A — Modulus inside the integral

## Question 1 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$12$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

Let $A=\int_{-2}^{0}f$, $B=\int_{0}^{2}f$. *Since $xf(x)>0$, $f<0$ on the left and $f>0$ on the right, so
$\int|f|=-A+B$.* Thus $A+B=10$ and $-A+B=14$ **(M1)**. Adding, $2B=24$ **(A1)**, so $\int_{0}^{2}f=B=12$
**(A1)**.
:::

## Question 2 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$12$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Because $f\le5$, $|f-5|=5-f$ — the modulus drops with no casework.* $\int_0^4(5-f)=8\Rightarrow
5\cdot4-\int_0^4 f=8$ **(M1 A1)**, so $\int_0^4 f=20-8=12$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 3 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$-7$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Fold: $\int_{-3}^{0}g(|x|)\,dx=\int_{0}^{3}g(t)\,dt=B$.* With $A=\int_{-3}^0 g$, $B=\int_0^3 g$: here
$xg(x)<0$ so $g>0$ on the left and $g<0$ on the right, giving $\int|g|=A-B$. Thus $A+B=-4$ and $A-B=10$
**(M1)**. Subtracting, $2B=-14$ **(A1)**, so $\int_0^3 g=B=-7$ **(A1)**.
:::

# Section B — Self-referential integral equations

## Question 4 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$\dfrac{36}{7}$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Let $k=\int_{-1}^{1}f$; integrate both sides over $[-1,1]$.* On the left,
$\int_{-1}^1 f+2\int_{-1}^1 f(-x)\,dx=k+2k=3k$ (using $\int f(-x)=k$) **(M1 A1)**. On the right,
$\int_{-1}^1 6\,dx=12$ and $\int_{-1}^1 x^2\,dx=\tfrac23$, giving $12+\tfrac23 k$ **(A1)**. So
$3k=12+\tfrac23k\Rightarrow\tfrac73k=12\Rightarrow k=\dfrac{36}{7}$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 5 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$f(1)=\dfrac13$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*$f$ odd ⇒ $f(-x)=-f(x)$, so the left side is $2f(x)+f(x)=3f(x)$.* With $k=\int_{-1}^1 t^2f(t)\,dt$,
$3f(x)=x^3+k\Rightarrow f(x)=\dfrac{x^3+k}{3}$ **(M1 A1)**. Substituting back,
$k=\tfrac13\int_{-1}^1(t^5+kt^2)\,dt=\tfrac13\bigl(0+\tfrac23k\bigr)=\tfrac29k$ **(A1)**, so $k=0$. Hence
$f(x)=\dfrac{x^3}{3}$ and $f(1)=\dfrac13$ **(A1)**.
:::

# Section C — Splitting, shifting & scaling

## Question 6 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$10$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Shift the second integral: $\int_0^1 f(x+2)\,dx=\int_2^3 f=4$* **(M1 A1)**. Then
$\int_0^3 f=\int_0^2 f+\int_2^3 f=6+4=10$ **(A1 A1)**.
:::

## Question 7 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$55$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Collapse $\int_0^r f=\sum_{n=0}^{r-1}(2n+1)=1+3+5+\dots=r^2$ (sum of the first $r$ odd numbers)* **(M1 A1)**.
So $\sum_{r=1}^{5}\int_0^r f=\sum_{r=1}^5 r^2=1+4+9+16+25$ **(A1)** $=55$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 8 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$5$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Substitute $u=2x$, $du=2\,dx$; as $x:0\to2$, $u:0\to4$.* $\int_0^2 f(2x)\,dx=\tfrac12\int_0^4 f(u)\,du$
**(M1 A1)** $=\tfrac12(10)=5$ **(A1)**.
:::

# Section D — Sequences of functions

## Question 9 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$1$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Build $f_3$ by cases on $[0,2]$.* $f_2(x)=|x-1|$; then $f_3(x)=\bigl||x-1|-1\bigr|$ **(M1)**.

- On $[0,1]$: $|x-1|=1-x$, so $f_3=|1-x-1|=x$.
- On $[1,2]$: $|x-1|=x-1$, so $f_3=|x-1-1|=2-x$. **(A1)**

*So $f_3$ is a "tent":* $\int_0^2 f_3=\int_0^1 x\,dx+\int_1^2(2-x)\,dx$ **(A1)** $=\tfrac12+\tfrac12=1$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 10 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$16$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Each step adds $\int_n^{n+1}2x\,dx=\bigl[x^2\bigr]_n^{n+1}=(n+1)^2-n^2=2n+1$* **(M1 A1)**. So
$b_2=1+3=4$, $b_3=4+5=9$, $b_4=9+7=16$ **(A1)**. *(The pattern is $b_n=n^2$.)* **(A1)**
:::
